findings: The answer preserves the source's explicit top-25%-by-purchase-volume objective and its PERCENT_RANK()/NTILE(4) hint, while clearly separating the assumed purchase_events(user_id, quantity) schema and SUM(quantity) metric from recovered source facts.
The SQL has the correct two-stage grain: detail rows are first aggregated to one purchase quantity per user, then a descending window rank is computed over users before applying the 0.25 cutoff.
The deterministic SQLite fixture validates an eight-user baseline, top-value ties, multiple purchase rows per user and the one-user boundary against the exact candidate contract.

The answer does not falsely equate PERCENT_RANK and NTILE: it explicitly explains the tie-preserving percentile-rank tradeoff versus near-equal row buckets and warns that a percentile threshold does not guarantee an exact 25% headcount.

Metric definition, refund/statistical-period questions, final ordering and strict-headcount tie-breaking are treated as boundaries or variants, and no production facts or personal experience are fabricated.
